question: Which Next.js tools help image performance?
shortAnswer: `next/image` for responsive sizes, lazy loading, modern formats, and CLS prevention.
detailedAnswer: Always set dimensions/aspect. Avoid shipping huge unoptimized images. Configure remotePatterns for external loaders.

question: How does next/font improve performance?
shortAnswer: Self-hosts fonts, reduces layout shift, and avoids render-blocking third-party font CSS.
detailedAnswer: Subset fonts. Limit weights. Prefer variable fonts when appropriate.

question: What causes large client bundles in Next apps?
shortAnswer: Root-level 'use client', heavy UI libs in client trees, barrel imports, and unnecessary polyfills.
detailedAnswer: Analyze with bundle analyzer. Push boundaries down. Prefer RSC for data display.

question: How do you optimize data fetching waterfalls?
shortAnswer: Fetch in parallel, compose with Suspense, cache shared lookups, and avoid sequential awaits when independent.
detailedAnswer: Lift common fetches or use Promise.all. Watch component trees that await parent-before-child unnecessarily.

question: Explain good loading UX with streaming.
shortAnswer: Shell + skeletons via loading.tsx/Suspense; prioritize above-the-fold content.
detailedAnswer: Don't block chrome on slow widgets. Measure LCP element ownership.

question: When is Edge rendering a performance win?
shortAnswer: When work is light and close to users; not when Node-heavy ORMs dominate.
detailedAnswer: Geo/auth redirects shine at Edge. Heavy SSR may be better on Node near the DB (regional).

question: Lead: set performance budgets for a Next.js org.
shortAnswer: Budgets for JS KB, LCP/INP, TTFB by route class; CI checks; RUM dashboards; ownership per template.
detailedAnswer: Classify routes (marketing vs app). Block regressions in PRs. Pair budgets with caching SLOs.
